alternatives.argument: Complete local replacement proof: write each component of the polynomial vector field as a finite monomial sum; the factorization a^q-b^q=(a-b)Σ_{j=0}^{q-1}a^{q-1-j}b^j and telescoping over the finitely many coordinates and monomials gives a local Lipschitz bound. On the assumed radius-R trajectory, the explicit finite polynomial coefficient sum M_R bounds ||F(x(t))||. The vector-valued FTC bound then gives ||x(t)-x(s)||≤M_R|t-s|, so x(t) is Cauchy at the finite endpoint; Euclidean completeness supplies x_* and the same estimate gives x(t)→x_*, with ||x_*||≤R. Picard–Lindelöf at (T_*,x_*) gives a local restart y. The old and new curves satisfy their oriented Volterra equations; continuity of F extends the old integral to T_*, and joining at the common value x_* adds the integral identities. The joined curve therefore satisfies the Volterra equation and is C^1 by the IVP–Volterra equivalence, giving an extension beyond T_* that agrees with x before T_*. This is the complete argument in local proof steps 1.1–5.1; the citation is not used as a proof substitute.
